Privileged programs are supposed to be able to read uninitialized stack
memory (ever since 6715df8d5) but
were permitted inconsistently. In particular
above state->allocated_stack
column2: but not below it. In other words

column1: stack was already ""large enough""
otherwise the access was rejected instead of being allowed to ""grow the

- in check_stack_slot_within_bounds()
- in check_stack_range_initialized()
This patch arranges for these accesses to be permitted. A bunch of tests
that were relying on the old rejection had to change; all of them were
changed to add also run unprivileged
column2: in which case the old behavior

column1: persists. One tests couldn't be updated - global_func16 - because it
can't run unprivileged for other reasons.
This patch also fixes the tracking of the stack size for variable-offset
reads. This second fix is bundled in the same commit as the first one
because they're inter-related. Before this patch
using registers containing a variable offset (as opposed to registers
with fixed
column2: known values) were not properly contributing to the

column1: function's needed stack size. As a result
column2: it was possible for a program

column1: to verify
column2: but then to attempt to read out-of-bounds data at runtime

column1: because a too small stack had been allocated for it.
Each function tracks the size of the stack it needs in
bpf_subprog_info.stack_depth
update_stack_depth(). For regular memory accesses
was calling update_state_depth() but it was passing in only the fixed
part of the offset register
column2: ignoring the variable offset. This was

column1: incorrect; the minimum possible value of that register should be used
instead.
This tracking is now fixed by centralizing the tracking of stack size in
grow_stack_state()
column2: and by lifting the calls to grow_stack_state() to

column1: check_stack_access_within_bounds() as suggested by Andrii. The code is
now simpler and more convincingly tracks the correct maximum stack size.
check_stack_range_initialized() can now rely on enough stack having been
allocated for the access; this helps with the fix for the first issue.
A few tests were changed to also check the stack depth computation. The
one that fails without this patch is verifier_var_off:stack_write_priv_vs_unpriv.
